authors: Codex research session; design frozen before any harness timing
question: On each of five fixed public prime-order toy curves, is the existing paired x-coordinate blocked BSGS implementation faster in cold one-target elapsed time than the existing tuned one-thread batched negation-map Pollard rho implementation when both solve and independently verify the same target and every BSGS table cost is charged? [pcc:unverified]

claims.text: For each curve separately, paired blocked BSGS has lower cold one-target elapsed time than tuned one-thread rho only when every scalar is correct, no row is censored, both same-instrument A/A intervals contain one, and the 95% paired-bootstrap interval for sum(rho total)/sum(BSGS total) lies wholly above one.
claims.if_supported: A host-, compiler-, implementation-, and size-specific constant-factor cold timing advantage on that curve.
claims.if_not_supported: The curve is reported as unresolved or as a BSGS loss; no faster-than-rho conclusion is made.

claims.text: A gain of at least ten percent on a curve is reported only when the lower endpoint of the same primary interval exceeds 1.10 and all correctness, censoring, and A/A gates pass.
claims.if_supported: At least a ten-percent host-specific cold timing advantage for the measured implementations on that curve.
claims.if_not_supported: No ten-percent claim; a smaller supported advantage may still be reported under C1.

claims.text: The 64-target shared-table panel is a separately labelled amortized implementation comparison and never licenses the cold one-target claim.
No asymptotic-exponent, memory-neutral, universal, production-key, or external-target conclusion is admissible from this study.

hypotheses.statement: Paired blocked BSGS has lower cold one-target elapsed time than tuned one-thread rho on at least some registered sizes despite its square-root memory cost.
hypotheses.mechanism: A prior arithmetic accounting suggested a possible constant-factor advantage, but it did not measure matched wall time and is not outcome evidence.

predictions.minimum_effect: For a curve, the two-sided 95% paired-bootstrap interval has lower endpoint above 1.0 after all correctness, censoring, and A/A gates pass.

data_seen.measured: Frozen design and source inspection only; no matched harness timing.

provenance.decisive_scope: Five fixed public 24-, 28-, 32-, 36-, and 40-bit prime-order toy curves under the frozen native-L2 protocol.

predictions.minimum_effect: Both BSGS and rho A/A 95% intervals contain 1.0.

provenance.decisive_scope: Same-instrument timing stability on the admitted host.

arms.description: Tuned batched negation-map Pollard rho, one thread, target-dependent setup and evaluator check charged.
Paired x-coordinate blocked BSGS with cold table allocation, build, search, deallocation, and evaluator check charged.
Second identical cold BSGS invocation on each bsgs-aa target; copy orientation is invocation-2 over invocation-1.
Second identical rho invocation with the same walk seed on each rho-aa target; copy orientation is invocation-2 over invocation-1.

flags.seed: same derived rho-walk seed as invocation 1

arms.description: One paired BSGS table built per batch and reused for 64 independently derived targets; secondary panel only.
Sixty-four sequential one-thread rho invocations per secondary batch, with all target-dependent setup charged.

positive.not_applicable_reason: Every measured row is itself a known-answer correctness fixture: the evaluator retains k, constructs Q=[k]G independently, and rejects any returned scalar that does not regenerate Q.

negative.not_applicable_reason: The question is a paired timing comparison of exact solvers, not detection against a null population.

factors.name: solver implementation
factors.how: Both solvers receive the same independently prepared target within every cold pair.

factors.name: execution order
factors.how: Even cold replicates run BSGS then rho; odd replicates run rho then BSGS. A/A invocation labels likewise alternate by parity.

factors.name: thread count
factors.how: Each solver is pinned to one workload CPU with RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1.

factors.name: curve size
factors.how: Every panel is run separately on every curve and conclusions remain separate by curve.

factors.name: target and rho-walk randomness
factors.how: All seeds are deterministically derived from the precommitted 256-bit master seed in separate domains before timing.

comparisons.reason: End-to-end implementation comparison on the same target; table build and target-dependent setup are charged.
Two identical cold BSGS invocations on each of 64 dedicated targets per curve.
Two identical rho invocations with the same walk seed on each of 64 dedicated targets per curve.
Deliberately separate secondary throughput panel; it cannot substitute for the cold one-target comparison.

randomization.arm_order_reason: Deterministic parity balancing was frozen before data: each solver leads 256 of the 512 cold pairs per curve.

seed_derivation.note: SHA-256 KDF and every domain, range, extraction rule, duplicate refusal, and bootstrap selection rule are frozen in seed-manifest.json. Addendum 2 changes only the lossless physical encoding of the complete mapping to derived-seeds.json schema blocked-bsgs-rho-wall/derived-seeds/v2.

instance_sampling.rule: Five fixed registered public curves; target scalar k=1+(derived_u64 mod (n-1)) in each frozen panel identity; no target is rerolled, dropped, or silently repeated.

blinding.how: Solver identity is needed to invoke different APIs; analysis, thresholds, target streams, and scheduling were frozen before any harness timing.

power.note: The fixed 512-pair sample per curve targets interval precision, not a claimed prospective power calculation. Curves are reported separately and no family-wide conclusion is licensed.

primary.name: Cold rho-to-BSGS ratio of arithmetic-mean elapsed time
primary.definition: For each curve, sum of 512 correctness-checked rho charged totals divided by the sum of the paired 512 correctness-checked cold BSGS charged totals; fixture construction and serialization are excluded.
primary.source: Native analyzer over event-sourced cold-paired result rows

secondary.name: Per-arm cold charged elapsed time
secondary.definition: BSGS includes allocation, build, search, candidate verification, evaluator check, and deallocation; rho includes target-dependent table, walks, collision recovery, internal check, and evaluator check.
secondary.source: Integer total_ns in each result event

secondary.name: Arithmetic mean paired elapsed-time difference
secondary.definition: Arithmetic mean over cold pairs of rho_total_ns minus bsgs_total_ns, separately by curve.
secondary.source: Native analyzer over cold-paired result rows

secondary.name: Elapsed time normalized by square-root group order
secondary.definition: Mean charged total elapsed time divided by sqrt(n), separately for each arm and curve.
secondary.source: Native analyzer and fixed curve order

secondary.name: Same-instrument invocation-2 to invocation-1 ratio
secondary.definition: For each curve and solver, sum of invocation-2 total_ns divided by sum of invocation-1 total_ns over 64 dedicated A/A pairs.
secondary.source: Native analyzer over bsgs-aa and rho-aa result rows

secondary.name: Secondary 64-target batch rho-to-BSGS elapsed ratio
secondary.definition: Per curve, ratio of summed rho batch totals to summed BSGS batch totals over 16 whole batches; bootstrap resamples batches, not targets.
secondary.source: Native analyzer over amortized-B64 batch result rows

secondary.name: Memory and exact implementation counters
secondary.definition: BSGS planned table bytes and every BsgsFastStats field; rho DP counts, every RhoResult and RhoOpCounts field; process peak RSS where available.
secondary.source: Per-arm result events and host envelope
secondary.resolution: one byte or one counted operation

record: canonical target coordinates and derived seed identities
measurement.timed_primary_justification: This is an end-to-end comparison of two existing implementations with different Montgomery backends and memory behavior; their internal operation counts are not a common cost unit. Native L2 isolation plus two same-instrument A/A panels are required before the monotonic clock can support the host-specific conclusion.

stopping_rules.rule: Stop after the fixed panel sizes on all five curves; never add, reroll, drop, or silently repeat a scientific row.
Stop the job at 3600 seconds, 4 GiB resident memory, or the USD 2.00 study ceiling; preserve partial intent/result events.
Reject before timing on a source, manifest, binary, curve, target-coordinate, thread-count, seed-duplication, or writable-evidence-store mismatch.

decision_rule.text: For each curve separately, report BSGS faster only when every scalar passes independent evaluation, no row is censored, both solver A/A intervals contain 1.0, and the type-1 two-sided 95% paired-bootstrap interval for sum(rho total_ns)/sum(BSGS total_ns) has lower endpoint above 1.0. Report at least ten percent only when that lower endpoint exceeds 1.10. Otherwise report unresolved, loss, or invalid as dictated by the interval and gates.
decision_rule.threshold: Primary lower CI endpoint >1.0; ten-percent lower CI endpoint >1.10; both A/A intervals must contain 1.0.
decision_rule.statistic: Per-curve ratio of sums of paired cold elapsed totals, with arithmetic mean paired difference reported beside it.
decision_rule.interval: 10,000 whole-pair percentile-bootstrap resamples; type-1 empirical quantiles at sorted zero-based indices 249 and 9749. A/A uses invocation-2/invocation-1; amortized analysis resamples whole batches.
decision_rule.effect_size_measure: rho elapsed divided by BSGS elapsed; values above one favor BSGS

inputs: derived seed mapping and compact bootstrap stream digests
source, build, binary, and host manifests
outputs: per-curve primary and A/A bootstrap summaries
benchmark record and raw artifact manifest

invalidation_rules: Any incorrect scalar or unequal canonical target construction blocks a positive result on that curve.
Any unmatched intent, solver failure, cap, timeout, panic, malformed row, or external interruption is explicit censoring and blocks an unconditional positive result on that curve.
Any source, manifest, lockfile, binary, curve, seed, thread-count, isolation, or evidence-store mismatch rejects the timed run.
A failed BSGS or rho A/A gate blocks the primary timing conclusion on that curve.
A resumed measurement row has invalid wall time and cannot enter the primary estimate.
The secondary amortized panel cannot rescue a failed or unresolved cold one-target panel.
inadmissible: Any claim of a smaller asymptotic exponent or a generic algorithm that beats Pollard rho asymptotically.
Any memory-neutral conclusion; blocked BSGS uses O(sqrt(n)) memory while rho has much smaller state.
Any universal, production-key, external-target, non-prime-field, non-x86_64, multi-thread, or unmeasured-host conclusion.
Any positive conclusion from local smoke timing, contended timing, a failed A/A gate, censored rows, or only the amortized-B64 panel.
Any pooling of the five sizes into one headline conclusion or fitted asymptotic exponent.
